title: The records tree is materialised in place; the whole-directory rename swap is deleted
context: The unit was dispatched on the premise that a concurrent reader is refused because the ledger ref advances before records reach disk. That premise is wrong. The count-mismatch path logs an anomaly and returns ok at records.ts:244; it never refuses. The refusal has exactly one source, syncWorkingCopy failing, and under concurrency that failure is the directory rename inside swapRecordsTreeIntoPlace: two processes both rename records aside, and the second one's rename onto the now-populated directory fails ENOTEMPTY. The self-repair contradiction dissolved with it, because when the post-CAS disk write fails the stamp is never advanced, so the next read genuinely does re-materialise and write-path.ts:219 was telling the truth. The race was already filed in-repo as item S1 in docs/plans/2026-08-25-post-cutover-repair/FILED.md, with 9 hits across the full 512-run CI history and a proposed remedy word for word what the architect reached independently.
options: teach the test classifier to honour retryable true on the records-field refusal
close the ref-leads-disk window in write-path so the transient state cannot exist
delete the whole-directory swap and materialise in place with per-file atomic writes and a ref-guarded prune
outcome: The materialiser's whole-directory rename swap is removed; the ledger tree is now written into the records directory in place with per-file atomic writes, followed by a prune that deletes only paths the ref no longer carries and is guarded by re-reading the ref after listing the disk. The swap's sole justification was whole-tree read atomicity, which the read surface never provided, since readAllRecordFiles does an unsynchronised readdirSync then reads each file separately, so the swap was destroying cross-record consistency rather than protecting it; three distinct user-visible failures fell out of that one unsynchronised rename, including erasure of a record a concurrent session had already committed and written. Teaching the test classifier to honour retryable was rejected because it would encode a retry contract for a refusal that should not exist, and would oblige every real client, a second session or a teammate or an MCP caller, to carry that retry loop. The prune must list the disk before re-reading the ref: because a writer commits to the ref before writing the file, an unmoved ref proves no peer record is on disk that the ref lacks, and inverting that order reopens the erasure this change exists to close.
